subject: Weight search was tuning against a scorer the EA never runs - fixed; FINGERPRINT data prerequisite solved offline; MT4 launch blocked
body:
Two warrants shipped, one real contamination fixed, and your FINGERPRINT document
unblocked the thing that has been blocking C3.1 for weeks. One thing needs you.

THE CONTAMINATION. CalculateScoreWithWeightsEx looked like a duplicate scorer. It was worse than
that. Every caller of it is a WEIGHT SEARCH - and it composed the score differently from the
function that actually trades: no synergy bonus, no type-aware adjustment, an extra multiplier
nothing else has, and it took its signal direction from the unweighted components, so volume,
volatility and session could carry the opposite sign on the same bar. So the system was choosing
weights that were optimal for a scoring function the EA never runs, then handing those weights to
the live scorer. It is now a wrapper that delegates. That is FORGE_FINALE's outstanding
score-function divergence contamination, closed at the root.

I ALMOST GAVE MYSELF A FALSE PASS. My corrected checker first reported C1.1 MET, because it had
decided the live scorer was a wrapper of the calibration scorer. It is not - live is 876 lines of
its own composition. It calls the other one exactly once, deep inside, as a sensitivity probe whose
value it never returns, and my rule counted "calls" as "delegates". One probe inverted the whole
authority order. A wrapper now has to actually return the other function's value. C1.1 stays NOT MET,
which is correct.

I ALSO BROKE C2.3 AND CAUGHT IT. My two new human log lines were 208 and 262 characters against your
160 limit. The board caught it because I re-ran it instead of assuming. Back to 70 of 70 passing.

YOUR FINGERPRINT DOCUMENT. You were right that it helps substantially. It specifies exactly the
payoff tracking C3.1 has been blocked on - outcome as realised size against the stop, worst dip on
every run whether traded or not, 320 exits scored in one pass, and critically scored by return
divided by the stop each one needed rather than raw return. I confirmed the stop-needed formula
against your own worked table (worst dip x 1.2).

AND I SOLVED ITS DATA PREREQUISITE WITHOUT THE TERMINAL. The exit search needs each run's real path.
Our score export cannot give that - its dip columns are computed over a fixed 20-bar window, the same
artefact that once made a large-target edge appear where there was none. Faking a path from returns
would understate the worst dip, which is the exact number the whole method divides by. So I now read
MT4's .hst history files straight off disk:

  USDJPY M5   111,548 bars   (our export has 50,000)
  EURUSD M5   133,098 bars   another market
  GBPUSD M5    88,982 bars   another market
  USDJPY M15   19,552 bars   another speed

That is 2.2x the runs, plus the second market and second speed your recurrence test demands - which
this campaign has never had, and which is the shared cause behind C4 being UNDERPOWERED. FP-25 says
none of it needs the terminal, and it does not.

ONE THING NEEDS YOU. Launching MT4 was denied by the permission system, twice. I did not route
around it - a scheduled task or VBS launcher would have been circumventing the block rather than
solving it. So the validation run has not happened: 28 warrants are shipped but unvalidated, and
C1.1 cannot flip because its evidence file only gets written when the EA runs. I verified the active
account first: 22650819 on XMGlobal-Demo, and the chart already targets SLS(181) with a 90-minute
cap. When you have a moment, either approve terminal launches or start MT4 yourself and I will take
it from there.

Board: 17 met, 7 not met. Continuing on the exit search, which needs nothing from you.
